title: An Extended-Reality App Using Motion Capture for Bending-Active Structure
summary: A collaborative feedback loop between physical bamboo, adaptive digital geometry and XR assembly guidance.
introduction: I worked with Wataru Nomura to bring measured physical conditions into the digital design and assembly process. Motion capture, adaptive modelling and a mobile XR interface connect changes in bamboo geometry with decisions made during assembly.
context: MAS in Architecture and Digital Fabrication, ETH Zürich · 2024 research project

context.title: Physical conditions become design inputs.
paragraphs: A fixed XR overlay cannot account for every bend or contact in natural bamboo. The research connects measured site conditions to an adaptive digital model, then returns updated geometry to the assembler.

method.title: A model that can receive and return information.
paragraphs: Reflective markers and OptiTrack supply position information. Rhino, Grasshopper, Python and Kangaroo support the adaptive geometry; an extension to COMPAS XR connects it to the Unity app through MQTT and Firebase.
My development work included MoCap interface and event updates, measurement-frame and circle visualisation, and rod-coordinate and colour-data output between Rhino/COMPAS and the app.

prototype.title: Adapt. Assemble. Join.
paragraphs: Three original app recordings show different tasks: repositioning a foundation control, viewing rod feedback during module assembly, and guiding connections between modules. Each recording retains its own original action and duration.

making.title: From the digital model to bamboo modules.
paragraphs: The chosen form is divided into Y-shaped units and converted into a strip-weaving pattern. The physical work combines marker-equipped rods, the mobile interface and manual assembly.

contributionNote: With Wataru Nomura, I researched motion-capture feedback, adaptive modelling and XR-guided bamboo assembly. My development work included MoCap interface and event updates, measurement-frame and circle visualisation, and rod-coordinate and colour-data output between Rhino/COMPAS and the app.
limitations: The original research records update delays, virtual-to-physical registration differences and image-target instability.
No controlled usability study or performance metrics established an improvement in assembly efficiency.
The CAD model preserves the selected original assembly geometry. It is not a new as-built survey, a stress analysis or a simulated deformation sequence.
The original app and tracking hardware have not been re-run or benchmarked for this website.

sourceNote: I explored how physical measurement, adaptive modelling and XR guidance could support bamboo assembly with Wataru Nomura. I worked across the research workflow and its digital tools, including MoCap interface updates, measurement visualisation and the exchange of rod geometry and colour data.
